You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: datanode-slownode-heartbeat-response
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/datanode-slownode-heartbeat-response.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/datanode-slownode-heartbeat-response.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: datanode-slownode-heartbeat-response" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/datanode-slownode-heartbeat-response.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/datanode-slownode-heartbeat-response.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"datanode-slownode-heartbeat-response","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

title: HDFS-16348. Mark slownode as badnode to recover pipeline
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  When a write pipeline keeps receiving acknowledgements from a slow DataNode, the client can remain stuck retrying the same unhealthy path instead of rebuilding around that node. Users want the pipeline to recover automatically before the write times out.


  ## Desired outcome

  Track repeated slow-node reports in the write pipeline and treat a DataNode as bad once it has been reported slow for the configured threshold of consecutive acknowledgements. At that point the client should abandon that node and recover the pipeline rather than waiting indefinitely for the same slow peer.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After a node crosses the slow-node threshold, pipeline recovery is triggered and the failure path clearly states that a reply was received from slowNode continuously for the configured number of times, instead of leaving the client on the degraded pipeline.

  '

=== slow-node-latency-reporting.yaml
title: HDFS-16582. Expose aggregate latency of slow node as perceived by the reporting node
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators investigating slow peers need more than a list of suspicious DataNodes; they need to see which reporter observed the problem and how much latency was involved.

  ## Desired outcome

  The slow-peer report should carry the reporting node and observed latency for each slow node, and the tracker should return structured `SlowPeerLatencyWithReportingNode` entries instead of plain strings.

  ## Acceptance signals

  `getSlowPeersReport()` includes host identities together with latency values such as the reported 15.5, 14.5, or 18.7-style measurements, and tracker queries retain per-reporter latency data.

  '
=== slow-datanode-metrics.yaml
title: HDFS-16526. Add metrics for slow DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators need clearer visibility into slow DataNode behavior so they can tell whether replication or write pipelines are being delayed by local disk work or by slow acknowledgements moving upstream through the pipeline. Without dedicated counters, these cases are harder to spot and diagnose from routine monitoring.


  ## Desired outcome

  DataNode metrics should expose separate counters for these slow-path conditions so monitoring systems can distinguish them directly. The exported metric contract needs to include `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` for delayed flush or sync activity and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` for delayed upstream acknowledgements, without changing normal write behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  DataNode metrics now publish `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount`, slow flush-or-sync events increment the former, slow upstream-ack events increment the latter, and the change adds observability only without altering the underlying pipeline semantics.

  '
=== slow-peer-outlier-metrics.yaml
title: HDFS-16595. Slow peer metrics - add median, median absolute deviation and upper latency limits
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators diagnosing slow peers need more than raw latency; they need the statistical context that made a peer an outlier.

  ## Desired outcome

  Slow-peer reporting should carry an `OutlierMetrics` record with `median`, `mad`, `upperLimitLatency`, and `actualLatency`, and those values should flow through reports, JSON output, and protobuf conversions.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Slow-peer reports and downstream consumers can see the exact metric values, not just the offending node names.

  '
=== namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure.yaml
title: HDFS-16528. Reconfigure slow peer enable for Namenode
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may want to turn slow-peer tracking on or off while a cluster is running so they can manage diagnostic overhead without taking the NameNode down. Right now the `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` setting is not fully reconfigurable on the NameNode side, which makes that operational toggle less useful than related live-reconfig options.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should allow `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` to be reconfigured at runtime, with slow-peer tracking behavior updating immediately to match the new boolean value. When disabled, slow-peer reports and JSON output should stop surfacing collected data; when enabled again, the normal slow-peer tracker should resume without requiring a restart.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` on a live NameNode, the NameNode switches between enabled and disabled slow-peer tracking behavior immediately, disabled mode returns empty slow-peer results instead of stale data, and invalid non-boolean values are rejected as reconfiguration errors rather than being silently accepted.

  '
